If you accept the argument that machine assisted proofs are valid then humans can at least try their hand at creating the shortest possible lean proofs, but if you decided that reading the proof base at all is meaningless then a minimized proof becomes worthless. It's not. It's probably pointless, but I will try to explain in layman's terms.

They perform computation that transforms the data into something new. In this case, answers that didn't exist before.

Think of it as compression. You take the sum total of all human knowledge (give or take a bit) and the prompt. Then you try to compress that data through the funnel of the prompt, and aftwards compare the result to correct (but novel) answer you created in advance. You train it to do this many times.

It eventually learns to compress all of that data in ways that produce correct answers, even when the answer was NEVER IN THE TRAINING DATA TO BEGIN WITH. It learns to derive new data from the existing data, because that's the only possible way for it to achieve the goal. Remember that many of the answers we are training it to produce didn't exist in the raw training data.

The way it calculates those answers is complicated and very mathy, so it's easy not to understand, but it's no parrot and the output has little relation to the input. Hell, you can run doom on the weights of an LLM. It's doing real, and transformative, computation that results in something very much new.

That's how it can do things like solve mathematical puzzles that humans have been stumped by for decades.

What if there is a non zero probability that it is a stochastic parrot anyway? Bayesian thinking and all that jazz.

Edit: I thought about it some more and AGI is the meta training loop where you train the model, run it, gather more data and then train again in a loop.

A stochastic parrot is a computer running inference. The stochastic parrot repeats a very complicated phrase or word: the model. The model weights themselves are like a complicated song that is sent from parrot to parrot. The parrot can also use the model weights to perform inference which gives it bounded intelligence, but for it to gain more capabilities it has to listen to a parrot with a better song.

I think we have to approach this situation with an open mind. Too many people want everything perfectly buttoned up on day one of a breakthrough like this, but that's never how breakthroughs have worked. For the Wiles proof of FLT there were seminars that had to be held just to get a relatively small number of experts in the world roughly up to speed with the proof strategy. Understanding of major results has never been anything close to instantaneous.

If anything, we will probably develop a deeper understanding of the proof of RH more quickly than we have for prior major proofs. And doing so will essentially be an engineering infrastructure project. Curious people around the world will direct their agents at simplifying and compressing the Lean source. This process will necessarily create a reverse theory-building process. Given how quickly agents can do this sort of work and how much interest there is in this problem, I'd expect understanding to develop from this approach quite fast.

I think we should expect future math proofs to feel more like this. The problems we and AI will increasingly tackle in math won't necessarily have a single key insight that led to their solution. Rather, they will be more like vast engineering projects that incorporate a multiplicity of ideas, techniques, and constructions that is just far beyond what humans could've brought together coherently. Even FLT felt less like one brilliant idea and more like a great infrastructure project around most of what was known in algebraic number theory and algebraic geometry at the time.

I refer you to Grothendeick's body of work, and his furious reaction to Delinge when Delinge rushed to prove the last of the Weil conjectures without having developed new theory that made doing it simple.

These AI proofs typically seem to have little new theory in the sense that Grothendieck would appreciate. It is the use of massive-scale search that applies existing theory.

children.author: Maxatar
children.text:
Among math circles there overwhelming consensus is that Masullo's proof is not remotely close to ready. Sadly as of the posting of his proof, a lot of it has been subject to formalization to verify if it's valid and as of today it contains 270 false claims, all of chapter 5 is invalid, it contains numerous unresolved steps and massive gaps in arguments.

This isn't like the paper just needs to be cleaned up and polished. A good chunk of the actual proof is simply not there and while it's certainly ambitious and also a credibly body of work, there's no reason to think that Masullo's work on this will pan out or that he's even headed in the right direction.

Too many people are talking about Masullo as if he basically has the proof in hand and just needs to tidy up some details here and there, similar to say when Andrew Wiles first published his proof of Fermat's Last Theorem (in which some flaws had been pointed out that Wiles had to correct) but that's simply not the case here. This work is so incredibly far from complete and it's not at all evident among the mathematical community that it will even lead to a proof of RH.

Publishing early gives him his cake and lets him eat it, too. He’s planted the flag and now can take the next 5 years working on this to polish and perfect and will be seen as the human who did it. Publishing the clean proof in that same time frame without this rushed pre-print landing on the same day wouldn’t earn him the same prestige. IMO smart move.

I personally think that the mistake here is to have been forced to publish. While the result of this proof (if correct) would be groundbraking I believe the true value is in understanding!

The computer can definitely say "yes" or "no" pretty much like an oracle could say it but 17m lines of Lean code tells absolutely nothing to the math community. Who's going to put effort to work on that? What progress does that bring to mathematics?

In contrast the attempted proof is "only" 940 pages that can be digested by human beings and I believe that's exactly the point of it. Even if incorrect perhaps there are many innovative techniques that can still applied elsewhere.

If I was Masullo I wouldn't have published anything because I would think that the work was still safe and with plenty of time to keep working on it.
